summary: In a fiction excerpt from a longer work titled 'Book 3', a narrator with a Betacam camera visits a room of infants in bassinets with Tara, who is dreamy and uncurious about where the babies come from. Tara says they are orphans or abandoned children brought from overseas, and she wants to take one out into the snow. The narrator refuses, and when she asks a changing attendant where a child came from, the woman stares in alarm and turns away. The narrator wonders whether Paula and Carly got their babies the same way.
one_line: A narrator filming a nursery of bassinet infants questions Tara about where the babies come from and gets evasive answers.
key_facts: The narrator films a room holding at least twenty bassinets, all alike, made of wicker with a white lace hood.
The room smells like baby powder.
Tara says the babies are orphans or abandoned children who come from overseas or elsewhere.
Tara says 'People bring them here' when asked how the children arrive.
Tara says 'The girls here take them to their new mothers' and that 'It's so sad to see them leave.'
Tara picks up an infant and says 'Isn't this one cute? I'd so love to have him.'
The narrator notes the light is not enough for broadcast-quality Betacam footage.
Ramala says the children are orphans or abandoned.
Tara says the nurses are made to try to speak English around the children, but they do not know much English.
Tara wants to take some babies outside into the snow to show them how beautiful it is.
The narrator refuses to take the babies out into the snow that night and suggests the morning instead.
The narrator notes that the baby being changed is a boy.
When the narrator asks the woman changing the baby where the child came from, she stares in alarm and turns away.
The narrator wonders whether Paula and Carly got their babies the same way.
